hint: Image problem or new image → set the image on the DEPLOYMENT (container name left of =)
cmds:
k describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
k get deployment <name> -o wide -n <ns>
k set image deployment/<name> <container>=<image> -n <ns>
k rollout status deployment/<name> -n <ns>

hint: Pod crashes or is not ready → logs of the LAST run, then describe (Last State, Exit Code, Events)
cmds:
k logs <pod> --previous -n <ns>
k describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
k edit deployment/<name> -n <ns>
k get pods -n <ns>

hint: Pod Pending → Events say why: requests too big, taint, nodeSelector, missing PVC
cmds:
k describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
k describe node <node>
k get pvc -n <ns>

hint: Rollback → history, then undo
cmds:
k rollout history deployment/<name> -n <ns>
k rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns>
k rollout status deployment/<name> -n <ns>

hint: Replicas → scale the deployment
cmds: k scale deployment/<name> --replicas=<n> -n <ns>

hint: HPA → autoscale with --cpu=<n>%; behavior (scaleUp/scaleDown) or memory targets only via YAML
cmds:
k autoscale deployment <name> --min=<n> --max=<n> --cpu=<n>% -n <ns>
k get hpa -n <ns>
k explain hpa.spec.behavior

hint: Service → expose; wrong traffic → compare selector/labels and targetPort with the endpoints
cmds:
k expose deployment --port=

--target-port= --type=NodePort -n k get endpoints -n k describe service -n k get pods --show-labels -n

hint: DNS → test from a pod with nslookup; service name.<ns>.svc.cluster.local
cmds:
k run tmp --image=busybox:1.36 --rm -it --restart=Never -n <ns> -- nslookup <svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local
k get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns

hint: NetworkPolicy → select target pods, allow by podSelector/namespaceSelector + port; no create shortcut for rules: write YAML
cmds:
k get networkpolicy -n <ns>
k get pods --show-labels -n <ns>
k get namespace --show-labels
k apply -f np.yaml

hint: Ingress → create ingress with --rule host/path=svc:port
cmds:
k create ingress <name> --rule="<host>/<path>=<svc>:<port>" -n <ns>
k describe ingress <name> -n <ns>

hint: Gateway API → Gateway (listener, TLS secret) + HTTPRoute (parentRefs, backendRefs); write YAML from the docs
cmds:
k get gatewayclass
k explain gateway.spec.listeners
k explain httproute.spec.rules
k apply -f gateway.yaml

hint: RBAC → serviceaccount, role, rolebinding, then prove it with auth can-i
cmds:
k create serviceaccount <sa> -n <ns>
k create role <role> --verb=get,list --resource=pods -n <ns>
k create rolebinding <rb> --role=<role> --serviceaccount=<ns>:<sa> -n <ns>
k auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> -n <ns>

hint: ConfigMap → create from literal/file, mount or envFrom, restart pods to pick it up
cmds:
k create configmap <name> --from-literal=<k>=<v> -n <ns>
k edit configmap/<name> -n <ns>
k rollout restart deployment/<name> -n <ns>

hint: Secret → generic or tls; check with describe (values stay hidden)
cmds:
k create secret generic <name> --from-literal=<k>=<v> -n <ns>
k create secret tls <name> --cert=<crt> --key=<key> -n <ns>
k describe secret <name> -n <ns>

hint: Storage → PVC must match a PV/StorageClass (size, accessModes, storageClassName); check Bound
cmds:
k get pv,pvc -n <ns>
k get storageclass
k describe pvc <name> -n <ns>
k explain persistentvolumeclaim.spec

hint: Default StorageClass → annotation is-default-class=true (remove it from the old one)
cmds:
k annotate storageclass <name> storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true --overwrite
k get storageclass

hint: Sidecar / init container → edit the deployment YAML; shared emptyDir volume for the log file
cmds:
k get deployment <name> -o yaml -n <ns> > d.yaml
k apply -f d.yaml
k logs <pod> -c <container> -n <ns>

hint: Taints → see them on the node, add a toleration to the pod, or remove the taint with -
cmds:
k describe node <node> | grep -i taint
k taint nodes <node> <key>=<value>:NoSchedule
k taint nodes <node> <key>=<value>:NoSchedule-

hint: Placement → label the node, nodeSelector/affinity in the pod spec
cmds:
k label nodes <node> <key>=<value>
k get nodes --show-labels

hint: Node maintenance → cordon/drain, then uncordon
cmds:
k drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
k uncordon <node>

hint: Node NotReady → kubelet on that node: status, logs, config, restart
cmds:
ssh <node>
systemctl status kubelet
journalctl -u kubelet -n 30 --no-pager
systemctl restart kubelet

hint: Control plane down → static pod manifests in /etc/kubernetes/manifests; crictl shows the containers
cmds:
crictl ps -a | grep kube-apiserver
crictl logs <id>
vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
journalctl -u kubelet -n 30 --no-pager

hint: etcd backup → etcdctl snapshot save with the 3 cert flags; check with etcdutl
cmds:
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save <file>
etcdutl --write-out=table snapshot status <file>

hint: Upgrade → kubeadm first, then kubelet + kubectl, one node at a time (drain/uncordon)
cmds:
kubeadm upgrade plan
kubeadm upgrade apply v<version>
kubeadm upgrade node
systemctl restart kubelet

hint: Helm → repo add, then install/upgrade or template; -n and --version from the question
cmds:
helm repo add <name> <url>
helm repo update
helm template <release> <repo>/<chart> --version <v> -n <ns> > out.yaml
helm install <release> <repo>/<chart> --version <v> -n <ns>

hint: Kustomize → build or apply -k on the folder
cmds:
k kustomize <dir>
k apply -k <dir>

hint: CRDs → list them, explain the fields, output exactly the format the question names
cmds:
k get crd
k api-resources | grep <group>
k explain <kind>.spec

hint: PriorityClass → create it, set priorityClassName in the pod spec
cmds:
k create priorityclass <name> --value=<n> --description="<text>"
k get priorityclass

hint: Output to a file → redirect exactly to the path in the question; check with cat
cmds:
k logs <pod> -n <ns> > /opt/<file>
cat /opt/<file>

hint: CNI → pod CIDR from kubeadm-config, then install the CNI from its docs
cmds:
k get configmap kubeadm-config -n kube-system -o yaml | grep -i podSubnet
k get pods -n kube-system

hint: Node prep → install package, enable service, sysctl params persistent in /etc/sysctl.d
cmds:
dpkg -i <file>.deb
systemctl enable --now <service>
sysctl --system

hint: Requests/limits → set resources on the deployment, then check the pods schedule
cmds:
k set resources deployment/<name> --requests=cpu=<c>,memory=<m> --limits=cpu=<c>,memory=<m> -n <ns>
k describe node <node> | grep -A6 Allocated
